title: Coherent finite-free coefficient comparison for ambient derived direct image
statement:
Let $q:Z\to W$ be a morphism of schemes, using small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $T=Z,W$, let $R_T\to S_T$ be maps of sheaves of commutative rings, with specified isomorphisms $q^{-1}R_W\cong R_Z$ and $q^{-1}S_W\cong S_Z$ commuting with these maps. Suppose $S_W$ is finite free as an $R_W$-module sheaf, meaning $S_W\cong R_W^{\oplus d}$ for some finite integer $d\geq0$. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(R_T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_T))$ and $D(S_T)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], canonical module pullback/direct-image adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and $C_T(M)=M\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $\mu:Lq_S^*C_W\xrightarrow{\sim}C_ZLq_R^*$ be the canonical balancing comparison of derived pullback and scalar tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For $M\in D(R_Z)$ define
$$\pi_{S/R,q,M}:C_WRq_{*,R}M\longrightarrow Rq_{*,S}C_ZM$$
to be the $Lq_S^*\dashv Rq_{*,S}$-adjunct of
$$Lq_S^*C_WRq_{*,R}M\xrightarrow{\mu}C_ZLq_R^*Rq_{*,R}M\xrightarrow{C_Z(\varepsilon_{R,M})}C_ZM.$$
Then $\pi_{S/R,q}$ is a natural isomorphism of exact functors $D(R_Z)\to D(S_W)$, including compatibility with the canonical cochain shift in the input $M$. In particular this is an equality of $S_W$-module derived morphisms, not just an equality after forgetting scalars.

For identity coefficient maps $R_T\to R_T$, it is the identity under the multiplication identifications. More generally let $R_T\to S_T\to B_T$ be a further compatible tower of ring sheaves, with $q^{-1}B_W\cong B_Z$, $B_W$ finite free over $S_W$, and all inverse-image identifications commuting with the coefficient maps. Write $C_{S/R,T},C_{B/S,T},C_{B/R,T}$ for the scalar functors and $a_T:C_{B/S,T}C_{S/R,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{B/R,T}$ for balanced associativity. For every $M\in D(R_Z)$ one has
$$\pi_{B/R,q,M}=Rq_{*,B}(a_{Z,M})\,\pi_{B/S,q,C_{S/R,Z}M}\,C_{B/S,W}(\pi_{S/R,q,M})\,(a_{W,Rq_{*,R}M})^{-1}.$$
No completeness, constructibility, properness or base-field hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply lem-sp-finite-free-scalar-shift to every scalar map on both sites. It proves the universal counit shift equation and triangulatedness for the exact specified left shifts. Apply lem-sp-finite-free-direct-image-shift to the actual direct-image comparison.

source.place: Tags 06YY, 07A6 and 0A8D; exactness and shift compatibility.

proof.text: Obtain eW, eZ and the columns from lem-sp-finite-free-direct-image-columns. Extensionality on finite biproduct inclusions identifies eW followed by restricted comparison and the restriction/direct-image isomorphism with mapBiproduct(Rq_R).inv followed by Rq_R(eZ.hom). Additivity of Rq_R makes mapBiproduct an isomorphism. Hence the restricted comparison is invertible. The conservativity clause of the ring-sheaf-change adjunct theorem reflects invertibility, objectwise and then for the natural transformation. Composite triangulatedness follows from the scalar and canonical direct-image triangulated instances. This works unchanged for d=0.

source.place: Tags 0944 and 07A6; finite-biproduct comparison and conservative restriction.

proof.text: For identity coefficients whisker the balancing square by the inverse target multiplication unit and source multiplication unit. The first equation of lem-sp-finite-free-balancing-coherence says this is the unitor identity square. mateEquiv_whiskerTop_whiskerBottom and mateEquiv_unitors give exactly the displayed comparison identity on every M.

source.place: Tags 0B56 and 0D6D; identity square and its mate.

proof.text: Horizontally compose the balancing squares for a and b and whisker by the inverse target derived associator and source derived associator. The tower equation of lem-sp-finite-free-balancing-coherence identifies this with balancing for a.comp b. Apply mateEquiv_whiskerTop_whiskerBottom and mateEquiv_vcomp. Evaluating at M gives exactly the inverse target associator, CW_b of the first comparison, the second comparison, and Rq_B of the source associator, in the required order. The finite-free assumptions are unnecessary for this equation.
